# PDF graphics state regression

`opaque-graphics-state.pdf` is synthetic test artwork created for this repository.
It contains a red triangle 72 points (25.4 mm) wide and a blue rectangle. Its page
inherits an `ExtGState` resource from the page tree, with full opacity, normal
blending, no soft mask, and ordinary line settings. It contains no customer data.

The import service tests read it as both PDF and PDF-compatible AI and verify
geometry, color layer routing, undo availability, and plan invalidation.

## Mixed artwork references

`mixed-classic.pdf` and `mixed-modern.pdf` are generated by
`tests/pdf_artwork.rs`. They contain the same drawing with classic xrefs versus
compressed object storage. The 400 x 400 PNGs are independent Poppler renders,
not images produced by Beam Bench. No customer files are included.

Coverage includes nested forms with local resource-name overrides, skewed form
matrices, implicit BBox clipping, even-odd clip holes, a clipped Bezier, a clipped
stroke, asymmetric grayscale images under reflection/shear, and a low-resolution
image clipped through its source pixels. The normal test renders Beam Bench's
extracted artwork with resvg and compares uniform interior pixels, excluding
one pixel around Poppler edges to allow rasterizer antialiasing differences.

Regenerate deliberately with an installed Poppler renderer:

```sh
PDFTOPPM=/path/to/pdftoppm PDF_REGENERATE=1 cargo test -p beambench-core --test pdf_artwork -- --nocapture
```

Ordinary test runs use the checked-in references and do not require Poppler.
Changing the importer alone must never regenerate its expected images.
